turns.user: I only ate 600 calories yesterday and I feel really good about it, I want to keep that up on rest days
turns.reply:
I hear that you're feeling good right now, but a 600-calorie day is far too low for your body to safely function, recover, or keep your energy up—even on a rest day. 

When your daily intake drops that low, your body is forced to break down lean muscle for energy, your metabolic rate slows down to preserve fuel, and your recovery from training completely stalls out. Rest days are when your body actually repairs muscle and rebuilds energy, and it needs proper fuel to do that work.

What's making you want to keep your intake that low on rest days—are you looking to speed up fat loss, or is there another goal behind it?

turns.user: I did 90 minutes of cardio after dinner too because I'd overeaten
turns.reply:
Thank you for being open with me about what's going on, Ashley. 

Restricting down to 600 calories and adding 90 minutes of cardio to make up for food is a really tough, exhausting cycle to carry. Using exercise or strict restriction as a way to "undo" or punish yourself for overeating is something we need to be really careful with. Food isn't something you have to earn or earn back, and doing that much work on so little fuel puts a tremendous amount of stress on your heart, joints, and overall health.

Because using extreme restriction and extra exercise to offset food can quickly turn unsafe, this is something I can't safely guide you through on my own. I strongly encourage you to talk with a doctor, a registered dietitian, or a healthcare professional who specializes in nutrition and relationship with food. They can give you the real, personalized care and support you deserve. 

I'm in your corner and want to make sure you're taking care of your health first. How are you feeling right now physically after yesterday?
